issue.title: Deep mode: delegating to a sub-agent (`task`) always fails with "StructuredTool does not support sync invocation"

steps: Please delegate this job to your general-purpose sub-agent rather than doing it yourself: the sub-agent should create the file report/total.txt containing only the sum of 17, 25 and 58.
expected: The task tool runs the general-purpose sub-agent, which creates report/total.txt containing 100.
defect: As soon as the model calls `task`, the turn fails with `Agent error: StructuredTool does not support sync invocation.`; the sub-agent never runs and no file is created.

fault location.explanation: The task tool is defined only as `async def` under @tool, producing a StructuredTool with a coroutine but no sync func, so any synchronous tool invocation raises 'StructuredTool does not support sync invocation'.
Deep mode runs the agent with sync agent.invoke(...), so the ToolNode calls tools synchronously and hits the async-only task tool.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). create_task_tool in agent/subagents.py defines the sub-agent delegation tool as `@tool(...) async def task(...)` and awaits `agents[subagent_type].ainvoke(sub_state)`. A LangChain StructuredTool built from a coroutine has no synchronous implementation. The deep-mode chat loop in cli/commands/chat.py drives the LangGraph agent with the synchronous `agent.invoke(...)`, so the prebuilt ToolNode invokes tools via the sync path and the task tool raises `StructuredTool does not support sync invocation`; the exception aborts the turn, the sub-agent never runs and report/total.txt is never written. Minimal fix: give the tool a sync implementation as well, e.g. build it with StructuredTool.from_function(func=sync_task, coroutine=async_task) where sync_task calls `agents[subagent_type].invoke(sub_state)`, or run the deep agent with `ainvoke`/`astream` (asyncio.run) in chat.py. The ABB binding also uses sync invoke, matching the CLI.
